
  ╭─────────────────────────────────────────────╮
  │  /hook  (/hooks)                            │
  │  Lifecycle Hooks                            │
  ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────╯

  Summary:
    Run your own shell commands on agent events.

  Usage:
    /hook            (interactive menu)
    /hook list
    /hook add
    /hook toggle     (arrow-key on/off switches)
    /hook remove     (pick from a list)
    /hook add <name> <event> <matcher> <command...>

  Details:
    Hooks run a shell command when an agent event fires. Events:
    pre_tool, post_tool, session_start, session_end, on_error.
    The matcher is a glob against the tool name (git_*, *, ...);
    session hooks always fire.
    
    Every action works without arguments: bare /hook opens a menu,
    and remove/on/off show a picker of your hooks.
    
    Each hook receives a JSON payload on stdin. A pre_tool hook
    that exits with code 2 BLOCKS the tool call and its stderr is
    shown as the reason. Hooks can only block actions — they can
    never approve, skip a confirmation, or bypass validation.
    A pre_tool hook that fails to run blocks the call (fail closed).

  Examples:
    $ /hook add test-gate pre_tool git_push pytest -q
    $ /hook add lint-after post_tool write_file ruff check .
    $ /hook off lint-after

  Tips:
    Tip: Hooks are stored in ~/.radsim/hooks.json (max 20).
    Tip: The command is everything after the matcher — no quotes needed.

  Related: /skill  /settings
